## Diagnosis

The `default`-namespace `app` Deployment had an init container `read-config` that checks in-cluster access to `configmaps/app-config`. Its pod spec requested `serviceAccountName: config-reader`.

```
Role app-config-reader  →  get /api/v1/configmaps   (restricted to resourceNames=[app-config])          ✓ least-privilege, unchanged
RoleBinding app-config-reader  →  roleRef Role/app-config-reader
    subject ServiceAccount name=app-reader        ← WRONG: no pod in this cluster ever uses SA "app-reader"
Deployment  →  serviceAccountName=config-reader   actual workload identity
```

So the Role existed with narrow scope, but its binding pointed at a non-existent ServiceAccount (`app-reader` doesn't exist; only `config-reader` exists). Result: `curl` from the init container failed `Error from server (403): configmaps "app-config" is forbidden`, `BackOff restarting failed container read-config`, `Init:Error` → pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, so `replicas=4`, `updatedReplicas=1`, `unavailableReplicas=1`.

## Change made

Single-field fix on the only RBAC object controlling the reader — alignment of the subject to the actual workload identity, no new permissions granted:

```
kubectl patch rolebinding app-config-reader -n default --type=strategic \
  -p '{"subjects":[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"config-reader","namespace":"default"}]}'
```

Role rules and all other settings (Deployment, ServiceAccount, ConfigMap) were left intact.

## Verification (fresh observations)

- RBAC: `rolebinding app-config-reader` now has subject `[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"config-reader","namespace":"default"}]`; only Role is `app-config-reader → configmaps[app-config] get`.
- Direct read from inside each running pod: `RC=0`, response `{"kind":"ConfigMap","apiVersion":"v1",...}` on all three pods (initContainer's exact same curl path, with CA + bearer token).
- Cluster check from the node side: `kubectl auth can-i --as=config-reader get configmaps/app-config -n default` → `yes`.
- Controller: Deployment shows `replicas=3 updated=3 ready=3 available=3`, no unavailable replica; old failing pod replaced and all three new pods `1/1 Running` with `RESTARTS=0` (old pod was the one in CrashLoopBackOff, now gone).
- No RBAC or workload objects beyond this were created/modified — age of both Role and RoleBinding equals their creation time, confirming only the subject line was touched.
